knowledge:
- key_parameters: snpdb=The database of trait-associated SNPs to use (e.g., taSNP or taSNPLD) ;; region=The query genomic intervals, provided as a data frame (with columns chr, start, end) or a GRanges object ;; snpdb.bg=The background SNPs database (e.g., CEU); if omitted, whole genome is used as background ;; rankby=Sorting criteria for results, either "pvalue" (increasing order) or "odds.ratio" (decreasing order) ;; test.method=Statistical test to use: "binomial" (default), "chisq", "fisher", or "nonparametric" ;; alternative=Hypothesis direction, "greater" (for enrichment, default) or "less" (for depletion) ;; keyword=Used in visualization/query functions to filter by trait/disease keyword ;; returnby=Used in queryKeyword to specify return format (e.g., "SNP")
- alternatives: chisq=Use when contingency table numbers are large and balanced ;; fisher=Use when contingency table numbers are small (e.g., no more than 20) ;; nonparametric=Use when the number of query genomic intervals is small (e.g., no more than 1000) ;; binomial=Default test method, not limited by sample size, distribution assumptions, or computational time
- when_to_use: When you have a set of genomic intervals (such as ChIP-seq peak regions, ATAC-seq peaks, or other genomic regions of interest) and want to determine if they are functionally connected with or enriched for specific traits or diseases based on GWAS data.
- pitfalls: Ensure genomic intervals are formatted correctly as a data frame with exact column names "chr", "start", "end" or as a GRanges object ;; Choosing an inappropriate statistical test method (e.g., using chi-square with very small counts) can lead to invalid p-values ;; Ensure the correct background is selected (whole genome vs. all SNPs) to match the underlying statistical assumptions.

workflows.name: gwas_snp_enrichment_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform enrichment analysis of trait-associated SNPs in genomic intervals and explore/visualize the results.
input: genomic_intervals.csv (data frame with columns chr, start, and end, or a GRanges object representing genomic intervals of interest)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the package and built-in databases ;; 2. Run enrichment analysis using traseR with chosen background and test method ;; 3. Print and inspect the enrichment results ;; 4. Visualize SNP functional class distribution using plotContext ;; 5. Visualize p-value distribution using plotPvalue ;; 6. Plot SNPs/genes in a specific genomic interval using plotInterval ;; 7. Query the database by keyword, gene, or SNP ID using queryKeyword, queryGene, and querySNP
workflows.code:
library(traseR)
data(taSNP)
data(Tcell)
x=traseR(taSNP,Tcell)
print(x)
x=traseR(snpdb=taSNPLD,region=Tcell)
print(x)
x=traseR(snpdb=taSNP,region=Tcell,snpdb.bg=CEU)
plotContext(snpdb=taSNP,region=Tcell,keyword="Autoimmune")
plotPvalue(snpdb=taSNP,region=Tcell,keyword="autoimmune",plot.type="densityplot")
plotInterval(snpdb=taSNP,data.frame(chr="chrX",start=152633780,end=152737085))
x=queryKeyword(snpdb=taSNP,region=Tcell,keyword="autoimmune",returnby="SNP")
head(x)
x=queryGene(snpdb=taSNP,genes=c("AGRN","UBE2J2","SSU72"))
x
x=querySNP(snpdb=taSNP,snpid=c("rs3766178","rs880051"))
x
